prompt: [Announcement — residence hall] What is the main purpose of Ms. Franklin’s announcement?
choices: To remind students about upcoming fire drills
To request volunteers for a maintenance project
To inform residents about a scheduled safety inspection and related procedures
To announce a change in residence hall entry policies
passage:
Transcript: Good morning, residents of Oakridge Hall. This is your Residence Life Coordinator, Ms. Franklin, with an important announcement regarding our annual fire safety inspection. As part of our ongoing commitment to your safety and compliance with university regulations, the inspection will take place this Thursday, March 12th, from 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. Maintenance staff, accompanied by a Residence Life representative, will enter every room in Oakridge Hall, including common areas and suites, to check smoke detectors, fire extinguishers, and ensure all emergency exits are accessible. To prepare, please make sure all personal belongings are cleared from doorways, hallways, and windowsills. Smoke detectors and fire extinguishers must not be blocked by decorations, posters, or furniture.

If you have a class or other commitments during the inspection window, you do not need to be present; however, you must leave your room unlocked between 8:45 a.m. and 2:15 p.m. For those concerned about valuables, you may store items in the front office, Room 101, by 8:30 a.m. Items can be retrieved after 3:00 p.m. on the same day. If you require special accommodations due to a documented disability or medical device, please email reslife@oakridge.edu no later than Tuesday, March 10th, at 12:00 p.m. After the inspection, a summary of findings and any necessary corrective actions will be posted on the first-floor bulletin board outside the lounge. Residents must resolve any violations within 48 hours. Your cooperation is essential to maintaining a safe living environment. Please follow these procedures carefully and reach out with any questions. Thank you for your attention and support.
explanation: The announcement details the timing, procedures, and special instructions for an upcoming fire safety inspection.
correct_answer: To inform residents about a scheduled safety inspection and related procedures

prompt: [Announcement — museum] What is one exception or special instruction mentioned for visitors with mobility needs?
choices: They are advised to avoid visiting during renovations
They must request a wheelchair at the information desk
They should wait for assistance at the main entrance
They should use the east elevator to reach Gallery F
passage:
Transcript: Good afternoon, visitors, and welcome to the City Art Museum. We appreciate your presence today and want to keep you informed about important changes to our weekend exhibit schedule. This announcement is brought to you by the information desk to ensure your visit is as smooth and enjoyable as possible. Due to ongoing renovations in Gallery C, the Impressionist Masters exhibit will be temporarily relocated. Starting this Saturday, May 14th, and continuing until further notice, the exhibit will be displayed in Gallery F, located on the second floor. Gallery F can be accessed via the east elevator, as the central elevator will be out of service during the renovation period. Please note that Gallery F has limited seating capacity, and for the preservation of our artwork, no food or drink is permitted inside the gallery.

Guided tours of the Impressionist Masters exhibit will now depart from the main lobby at 11:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m. every day, replacing the previous tour times. If you have purchased tickets online for this exhibit, your tickets remain valid; however, you are required to check in at the temporary ticketing desk set up near the elevators on the second floor before entering Gallery F. For visitors needing wheelchair access, please use the east elevator, which is fully accessible. If you have any questions regarding ticketing, accessibility, or the new exhibit location, please call our information desk at 555-0199 or visit our website at www.cityartmuseum.org. Thank you for your understanding and cooperation during these improvements. We encourage you to explore the Impressionist Masters exhibit in its new location and join a guided tour for a richer experience.
explanation: The announcement states that the east elevator should be used for wheelchair access because the central elevator is out of service.
correct_answer: They should use the east elevator to reach Gallery F

distractor_rationales.choice: They must request a wheelchair at the information desk
distractor_rationales.reason: No mention is made of requesting wheelchairs.

distractor_rationales.choice: They are advised to avoid visiting during renovations
distractor_rationales.reason: Visitors are not told to avoid visiting; alternative access is provided.

distractor_rationales.choice: They should wait for assistance at the main entrance
distractor_rationales.reason: No instruction is given to wait for assistance at the entrance.

prompt: [Announcement — museum] What is the main reason for requiring timed-entry tickets for the ‘Art Through the Ages’ exhibition?
choices: To increase ticket sales by moving every purchase onto the website
To manage capacity limits and ensure a safe experience
To give each guest a longer viewing window inside Exhibition Hall B
To keep walk-up tickets available for visitors who decide late
passage:
Transcript: Good afternoon, visitors, and welcome to the City Museum. We appreciate your interest in our upcoming ‘Art Through the Ages’ special exhibition, and we have some important updates regarding ticketing procedures and exhibit access to ensure a smooth and enjoyable experience for everyone. The ‘Art Through the Ages’ exhibition will run from Saturday, April 20th through Wednesday, May 15th, and will be located in Exhibition Hall B on the second floor. Please note that, due to anticipated high demand and to maintain a comfortable environment, all guests are now required to purchase timed-entry tickets in advance through our website at www.citymuseum.org/tickets. Walk-up ticket sales at the museum entrance will not be available during this period. Each ticket allows access for a specific two-hour window, with entry times beginning at 10:00 a.m.

and the last entry at 4:00 p.m. daily. We kindly ask that you arrive at least 10 minutes before your scheduled time, as late arrivals may not be accommodated due to strict capacity limits. Museum members receive a 20% discount on tickets but must also reserve their spots online. Families with children under six, or visitors requiring accessibility accommodations, should contact guestservices@citymuseum.org or call (555) 123-4567 prior to their visit for assistance with stroller access, wheelchair rentals, or special arrangements. If you need to reschedule, please use the link provided in your confirmation email at least 24 hours before your reserved time slot. After your visit, we invite you to complete our feedback survey, accessible via QR codes posted near the Exhibition Hall B exit. Thank you for your cooperation and for helping us provide a safe, memorable museum experience for all.
explanation: The announcement mentions capacity limits and safety as the reason for timed-entry tickets.
correct_answer: To manage capacity limits and ensure a safe experience

Transcript: Good morning, students and staff. This is the campus safety office with an important announcement regarding next week’s scheduled fire drills. To ensure the ongoing safety of our university community, mandatory fire drills will be conducted in all academic buildings on Thursday, April 6th. Drills will begin promptly at 10:00 a.m. and continue through 3:00 p.m. Each building—including Science Hall, Humanities Center, and the Library—will be evacuated once during this period. Specific drill times for each building are posted on the safety office website and on bulletin boards near main entrances. For example, Science Hall will be evacuated at 10:30 a.m., Humanities Center at 12:00 p.m., and the Library at 2:00 p.m.

Drills are expected to last approximately 20 minutes per building. When the fire alarm sounds, please exit immediately using the nearest stairwell, following the evacuation routes clearly posted near all exits. Do not use elevators during the drill under any circumstances. If you have mobility concerns or require assistance evacuating, please notify your building coordinator by 5:00 p.m. on Tuesday, April 4th, so that arrangements can be made in advance. Laboratory occupants must secure all hazardous materials and equipment before leaving. Classes and meetings will resume as soon as the drill concludes; faculty have been informed to accommodate students who may arrive late due to the drills. For further information, email safety@university.edu or call extension 4400. Your participation is essential for campus safety. Thank you for your cooperation and attention.
explanation: The announcement instructs those needing assistance to notify their building coordinator by Tuesday.
correct_answer: Inform their building coordinator by Tuesday

distractor_rationales.reason: Arrangements must be made in advance, not during the drill.

distractor_rationales.choice: Contact the campus safety office during the drill
distractor_rationales.reason: Contact should be made before the drill, not during.

distractor_rationales.choice: Use the elevator to exit quickly
distractor_rationales.reason: Elevators should not be used during fire drills.

Transcript: Good morning, passengers. This is an important service announcement from the City Transit Authority regarding upcoming changes to Blue Line service. We want to ensure your travel plans go smoothly, so please listen carefully to the following details. Due to essential track maintenance, the Blue Line will operate on a revised schedule this Saturday, April 19th, from 6:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. During these hours, trains will depart every 30 minutes instead of the usual 15 minutes. In addition, service between Central Station and Oakwood will be temporarily suspended. To assist you, shuttle buses will run between Central Station, Parkside, and Oakwood, stopping at the north exit of each affected station. Look for signs and uniformed staff at each location—staff will be available to answer questions and provide directions throughout the day.

If you are traveling to the airport, please allow at least an extra 20 minutes for your journey, as connections may be delayed. Regular fares remain in effect, and monthly pass holders may use their passes on the shuttle buses at no extra charge. For those needing wheelchair access, accessible shuttles are available—please notify a staff member at least 15 minutes prior to your departure time so we can accommodate you. For further information, visit our website at www.citytransit.com, or call our 24-hour hotline at 555-0199. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this may cause and thank you for your patience and cooperation. Please check the City Transit app for real-time updates and plan your trip accordingly. Safe travels to all.
explanation: The announcement states that trains will run every 30 minutes and a section will be served by shuttle buses.
correct_answer: Trains will run less frequently and part of the route will use shuttle buses

distractor_rationales.choice: All trains will be canceled for the entire day
Fares will be increased for all passengers
The Blue Line will only operate between Central Station and Oakwood
distractor_rationales.reason: That section is replaced by shuttles, not trains.

Transcript: Good morning, valued visitors, and welcome to the City Museum. This is an important announcement from the Visitor Services Department regarding an exciting upcoming event. We are delighted to announce that, in celebration of the much-anticipated Art and Innovation Exhibit, the museum will be extending its operating hours from Sunday, May 5th, through Sunday, June 2nd. During this period, the museum will be open daily from 9:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m., including both Saturdays and Sundays, to give everyone ample opportunity to experience this special showcase. Special guided tours of the Art and Innovation Exhibit will be offered each day at 11:00 a.m., 2:00 p.m., and 6:00 p.m. Tours will begin promptly in Room 204, located on the second floor.

Tickets for these tours can be purchased at the main information desk in the lobby for $5 per person, in addition to the regular admission fee. Please note that space is limited to 25 participants per tour, so early arrival is recommended. We would also like to remind all guests that photography is strictly prohibited in the Innovation Gallery, located in Room 210, due to copyright and licensing restrictions. Families visiting with young children are welcome to use our supervised play area, available near the west entrance in Room 105, open daily from 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. If you are planning to visit with a group of ten or more, please email groupservices@citymuseum.org to reserve your spot at least three days in advance. For more information or to purchase tickets online, please visit www.citymuseum.org. We encourage everyone to take advantage of these special offerings and wish you a wonderful visit!
explanation: Photography is prohibited in the Innovation Gallery due to copyright restrictions.

distractor_rationales.reason: A supervised play area is available for children.

distractor_rationales.choice: Purchasing tickets at the information desk
distractor_rationales.reason: Tickets can be purchased at the desk.
